question: persister

parallel.problem: Why do a small minority of firms in the same industry, facing the same tariff or demand shock, survive and grow while comparable peers exit?
parallel.how_studied: Economists link firm-level administrative or census panel data and run event studies around the shock. They match survivors and exits on characteristics observed before the shock, such as productivity, liquidity, customer concentration and management practices. Difference-in-differences designs and regression discontinuities around eligibility cutoffs separate advantages that existed beforehand from adaptive responses after the shock, such as product switching.

prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Economics
Problem: Why do a small minority of firms in the same industry, facing the same tariff or demand shock, survive and grow while comparable peers exit?
How it is studied: Economists link firm-level administrative or census panel data and run event studies around the shock. They match survivors and exits on characteristics observed before the shock, such as productivity, liquidity, customer concentration and management practices. Difference-in-differences designs and regression discontinuities around eligibility cutoffs separate advantages that existed beforehand from adaptive responses after the shock, such as product switching.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Sister-cell split design as a pre-shock administrative panel
ideas.description: Exploit the fact that a cell division produces two near-identical 'twins': profile one daughter destructively (scRNA-seq, proteomics, or a reporter snapshot) while its sister is exposed to the targeted drug and followed to a survival/death outcome, so the pre-shock covariate vector is measured on the same genetic and epigenetic unit whose fate is observed. This is the cancer-cell analogue of linking a firm's pre-shock census record to its post-shock exit status, and it cleanly separates predetermined advantage from post-treatment adaptation.

ideas.title: Event study with pre-trend testing on continuous single-cell trajectories
ideas.description: Use long-term live imaging with multiplexed signaling and stress reporters to build per-cell time series spanning days before drug addition through weeks after, then align all cells on the treatment date and estimate the survivor-versus-dier difference at each lead and lag. Significant differences at negative leads identify genuinely preexisting heterogeneity, while a flat pre-period with divergence only after exposure would show that survivorship is generated by the shock itself, and the pre-trend test guards against the parallel-trends violation that naive survivor-versus-dier comparisons ignore.

ideas.title: Matching survivors to dead peers on pre-treatment observables, then quantifying the unexplained residual
ideas.description: With barcoded clonal families profiled before treatment, construct nearest-neighbor or propensity-score matched pairs of future survivors and future dying cells balanced on cell-cycle phase, size, target-pathway activity, mitochondrial content, and local density, and test how much survival probability remains unexplained after balancing. The size and structure of that residual is itself the scientific result: it bounds how much of persistence is attributable to measured states versus unobserved or purely stochastic factors, exactly as economists bound selection on unobservables after matching on productivity and liquidity.

ideas.title: Regression discontinuity around a tunable target-dosage cutoff
ideas.description: Use a degron- or inducible-promoter-titrated level of the drug target (or of a candidate resistance mediator) as a continuous running variable, with a sharp kill threshold, and compare cells falling just above versus just below the cutoff where assignment is effectively as-good-as-random. This isolates the causal contribution of that one variable to survival, separating it from the many correlated states that confound a simple association between high expression and persistence.

ideas.title: Difference-in-differences across drug holiday and rechallenge to test whether the advantage is heritable or an adaptive pivot
ideas.description: Split each barcoded clone into treated and vehicle arms, then release survivors into drug-free medium, re-split, and rechallenge, estimating within-clone changes in survival relative to the never-treated arm of the same clone. A persistent within-clone shift indicates an inherited or epigenetically stabilized advantage, while reversion to baseline indicates a transient post-shock adaptive response — the direct analogue of distinguishing durable firm productivity from post-tariff product switching.
